top_categories.workout_context: 7,339ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

GFNY San Luis Potosí's high-altitude two-lap climbing course rewards road-specific control. Practice smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 95 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY San Luis Potosí's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before December.
77ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At GFNY San Luis Potosí, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
At mile 60 of 95, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY San Luis Potosí. Train it until it feels boring.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 95 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
7,339ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at GFNY San Luis Potosí. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on high-altitude two-lap climbing course can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 95 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for GFNY San Luis Potosí’s 95 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: GFNY San Luis Potosí with 7,339ft of climbing finishes high enough for reduced oxygen availability to affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. Start elevation around 1,877 meters.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at GFNY San Luis Potosí rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on high-altitude two-lap climbing course to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Road Specific, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 95 miles of high-altitude two-lap climbing course in San Luis Potosí, Mexico.
